passages.text: Religion is not in doctrines, in dogmas, nor in intellectual argumentation; it is being and becoming, it is realisation. We hear so many talking about God and the soul, and all the mysteries of the universe, but if you take them one by one, and ask them, “Have you realised God? Have you seen your Soul?” — how many can say they have? And yet they are all fighting with one another!
passages.note: Religious arguments versus lived spiritual experience

passages.text: When a jar is being filled with water, it makes a noise, but when it is full, there is no noise.
passages.note: Loud certainty versus quiet real knowing

passages.text: The world is full of the talk of love, but it is hard to love. Where is love? How do you know that there is love? The first test of love is that it knows no bargaining. So long as you see a man love another only to get something from him, you know that that is not love; it is shopkeeping. Wherever there is any question of buying and selling, it is not love.
passages.note: Whether love is real or transactional
